data.text:
Quezon City Pumping Station Sparks Political Storm

Quezon City Mayor Joy Belmonte has raised red flags over a pumping station project in Matalahib Creek, built by St. Timothy Construction. According to Belmonte, the structure—erected in District 1 under Rep. Arjo Atayde’s watch—was put up in a non-buildable area and even worsens flooding by narrowing the creek.

When asked, Cong. Arjo Atayde reportedly denied knowledge of the project at first. Belmonte said she is giving him the benefit of the doubt, but confirmed that the city is now investigating possible anomalies.

City Engineer Dale Perral disclosed that the LGU found the pumping station inconsistent with Quezon City’s flood-control master plan and has recommended its removal or redesign. The QC government has also moved to block a second proposed station in the district, citing the same risks.

Meanwhile, the controversy arises as St. Timothy Construction faces national scrutiny: President Marcos has demanded an explanation regarding alleged failed flood-control works, and Malacañang states that the contractor has yet to respond. An unfinished pumping station in Sto. Domingo, QC—also under St. Timothy—was exposed in the media just weeks earlier.

For Atayde, the optics are damaging: a defective project inside his own district, a mayor openly questioning its legality, and a contractor already blacklisted in the public eye. While he insists he never benefited from any contractor, the unfolding investigation may determine whether this is simply a DPWH blunder or a case of political complicity in Quezon City’s flood woes.
